publications.title: A threshold-sensitive framework for tracking Hypoxia recurrence across coastal ecosystems
publications.institution: School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences, Stony Brook University

observational_coverage.method: non-stationary generalized extreme-value models across multiple oxygen thresholds
observational_coverage.comparison: five co-located Chesapeake Bay benthic stations

findings: The proposed Hypoxia Recurrence Risk Indicator combines recurrence class, threshold sensitivity and bootstrap support rather than relying only on areal extent or one fixed criterion.
The reported gradients placed frequent severe low oxygen in western Long Island Sound, the Louisiana shelf, the Chesapeake Bay mainstem and upper Narragansett Bay.
The original recurrence classification was the most common bootstrap result in 93.3% of cases, but support was weaker for the frequent and infrequent classes.
publications.evidence_quality: Strong multi-system relevance and explicit bootstrap uncertainty, including a northern Gulf system, but this checkpoint could verify only the abstract and bibliographic identity rather than full methods or source-level station denominators.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Discrete monitoring can miss short-lived minima and therefore inflate inferred return periods.
Absolute recurrence values are not directly comparable when sampling cadence, depth, season and thresholds differ among systems.
The five-station Chesapeake comparison is not an independent Mobile Bay validation, forecast test or fish-event endpoint.
Annual summer minima cannot establish predawn duration, concurrent vertical gradients or Jubilee biology.
mobile_bay_implications: Use only as a method lead for threshold-sensitivity and recurrence uncertainty after local depth, cadence, QC and observation-effort gates are explicit.
Do not combine Sand Reef daily minima, profiles and continuous sensors as if they shared duration or sampling support.
Do not derive a Jubilee label or production threshold from a Gulf-wide hypoxia recurrence class.
offline_validation_opportunities: If sufficient local records become available, compare recurrence assignments across predeclared oxygen thresholds while preserving sampling cadence and depth.
Report bootstrap support and abstain where monitoring misses plausible short events or site transfer is unverified.

publications.title: Oxygen Dynamics Across Connected Coastal Ecosystems: Heterogeneity May Mitigate Oxygen Extremes
publications.institution: Department of Civil Engineering, School of Architecture and Urban Planning, Tokai University

observational_coverage.system: Fukido River coastal system, Ishigaki Island, Japan
observational_coverage.sampling: simultaneous 10-minute dissolved-oxygen saturation and environmental observations

findings: Coral-reef and seagrass oxygen variability was dominated by diel periodicity, while mangrove variability was primarily semidiurnal tidal with an additional diel component.
Maximum saturation reached 172%, 162% and 146% at the reef, seagrass and mangrove sites; the mangrove declined to 19.9% saturation.
Selected predictors explained 55.2% of dissolved-oxygen variance. Temperature was the strongest reported correlate, but the regression residuals retained substantial temporal autocorrelation.
publications.evidence_quality: High-resolution, simultaneous, open-data observational design with explicit statistics; limited to one tropical system and one 27-day period, without external or forecast validation.
uncertainty_and_limitations: The primary metric is oxygen saturation rather than concentration, and conversion depends on temperature and salinity.
The observational window is short and one season; the study does not establish interannual persistence.
The authors describe statistical correlates, not causal drivers, and note substantial temporal autocorrelation.
Connected sites still showed different oxygen regimes, so proximity does not justify station substitution.
mobile_bay_implications: The simultaneous-site result reinforces separate site identity, habitat, depth, clock and units before transferring oxygen evidence.
A high-frequency source should retain diel and tidal structure rather than being reduced to unmatched daily extrema.
This is contextual support for the existing Battleship-Meaher substitution gate, not a new feature or pier-mount decision.
offline_validation_opportunities: For verified local paired series, compare site-specific diel and tidal spectra before considering any common feature representation.
Require residual-autocorrelation-aware uncertainty and held-out time blocks for any local temperature/oxygen relationship.

publications.title: Temperature dependence and coupling of dissolved oxygen and pH in coastal habitats
institutions: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
Mediterranean Institute for Advanced Studies, CSIC-UIB
findings: Across the pooled dataset, higher temperature was associated with lower oxygen and pH and larger diel ranges, with extreme variability in warmer habitats.
Hypoxic and severely hypoxic observations occurred in mangrove, coral-reef and seagrass systems, while daytime supersaturation also occurred.
The authors explicitly characterize the relationships as emergent global patterns rather than strong predictive relationships at individual sites.
publications.evidence_quality: Large, geographically diverse, open full-text compilation with complete-cycle screening and data/code references; heterogeneous sensors, sampling intervals, habitats and nutrient regimes limit causal and site-specific interpretation.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Sampling intervals ranged from 5 to 60 minutes and instruments differed by site.
Nutrient inputs were unavailable across sites, preventing isolation of temperature from an important oxygen driver.
Pooling habitats and regions creates large residual heterogeneity and does not validate a Point Clear relationship.
Bulk-water observations may not represent organism boundary-layer exposure, bottom water or shoreline contact strips.
The paper does not evaluate Jubilee events, fish aggregation, issue-time forecasts or out-of-sample event classification.
mobile_bay_implications: Temperature should be treated as one interacting correlate and not as a portable causal calibration across sites.
Daily means or daytime samples can hide both nocturnal lows and daytime supersaturation; complete-cycle coverage remains essential.
If pH is later available locally, test it only as a co-measured state variable with site-specific calibration, depth and timing rather than a proxy replacement for oxygen.
offline_validation_opportunities: Within retained local records, compare complete 24-hour cycles across matched temperature, tide, wind, depth and habitat strata.
Test whether pH adds held-out information beyond temperature and direct oxygen only where synchronized local measurements and QA exist.

synthesis.new_scientific_finding: Three post-window studies independently reinforce that oxygen recurrence, spatial heterogeneity and diel temperature coupling depend strongly on threshold, site and cadence; none validates a Jubilee forecast, cross-site substitution or biological detection endpoint.
research_questions: Can local low-oxygen recurrence be estimated without cadence-driven missed minima, and is the result stable across predeclared thresholds?
Do verified Eastern Shore sites retain different diel/tidal oxygen regimes after matching depth, habitat, season and clocks?
Does synchronized local pH add held-out information beyond direct oxygen and temperature?
next_steps: Apply the ERDC three-day post-service gate and verify the August 22, 2024 Relic Shell masks/service clocks before any local oxygen acceptance.
Continue compact-JSON biological equivalence and provider-side actual billing acceptance ahead of wind-capture optimization.
unresolved_risks: No positive-event paired compact/original biological challenge set.
No validated local near-bed current geometry or direct Eastern Shore bottom-oxygen time series.
Regional oxygen sources still have material unit, service-clock, depth and spatial-transfer gates.
